title: What does TicketCreate do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of TicketCreate and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, TicketCreate reserves sequence numbers as Tickets so later XRPL transactions can be prepared without normal sequential submission. [1]

A transaction using a Ticket sets Sequence to zero and identifies the Ticket with TicketSequence. Tickets consume owner reserve while outstanding and are consumed when used according to transaction rules. This supports independent preparation; it does not permit reusing a consumed Ticket or charging the same purchase twice. [1]

The TicketCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using TicketCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
